claims.evidence: The seller admits it is faulty, and the witness observed 'inverter' printed on the outdoor unit.
The witness identified the brand as Sanyo from the front of the unit.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the specification plate (sticker) on the side of the indoor or outdoor unit.
risks.if_unproven: As a 1HP unit (the lowest value capacity).

risks.proof: A video clip of a technician performing a terminal continuity test or attempting to start the compressor.
risks.if_unproven: As a dead compressor (scrap value only).

risks.risk: Burnt or missing inverter PCB (control board)
risks.proof: A photo of the internal electronics compartment of the outdoor unit showing the board condition.
risks.if_unproven: As a missing or non-repairable board.

risks.risk: Internal component stripping (indicated by red handwriting/technician marks)
risks.proof: A video showing the internal components of both units to ensure motors and coils are present.
risks.if_unproven: As a stripped shell for parts.

proof_requests: Photo of the specification plate showing the model number and HP rating.
Photo of the side of the outdoor unit where the copper pipes connect.
Photo of the indoor unit with the front cover lifted to show the evaporator coils.
Photo of the remote control if available.
response.reason: The horsepower (HP) rating is missing, which is the primary factor for pricing a faulty unit in Lagos. The red handwriting suggests it has already been inspected or rejected by a technician.
